item: Basis: Family Code article 54 as amended by Ordinance 05-02 of 2005: the wife may separate herself from her husband by khul without his consent, for a financial consideration.

If the spouses do not agree on the consideration, the judge fixes it, without exceeding the value of the proper dowry (sadaq al-mithl) at the time of the judgment: check the amount offered and whether the husband accepts it.
Before the 2005 amendment the courts required the husband's consent; check that the claim relies on the amended text and does not plead consent as a condition.

Element to prove: a valid marriage between the parties, proven by an extract of the civil-status register (Family Code article 22); if the marriage is not registered, a judgment proving it is needed first or in the same claim.
Check whether the marriage was consummated: it matters for the idda, the maintenance during the idda and the dowry, not for the right to khul itself.

No cause or harm needs to be proved for khul; distinguish it from tatliq (judicial divorce at the wife's request for a cause listed in article 53), which needs proof of the cause and gives the wife damages.

Distinguish khul from divorce by mutual consent (CPCA articles on divorce by mutual consent: joint petition, agreement on effects) and from divorce by the husband's will (article 48, with possible damages for abusive divorce, article 52).
Dissolution only by judgment, after several reconciliation attempts by the judge, within a period not exceeding three months from the filing of the claim (Family Code article 49).
CPCA family-matters chapter: the reconciliation attempts are mandatory, the spouses attend in person, a record is drawn up; check the rules on a spouse who does not attend or lives abroad.
Competent section: the family affairs section (qism shu'un al-usra) of the tribunal (CPCA articles 423 and following); if the court has no section, the court itself hears the case.

Territorial jurisdiction: for divorce and its effects, the court of the place of the marital home; check the special rule for maintenance (place of the creditor) and custody (place of exercise of custody), and whether this jurisdiction is of public order (CPCA article 426 and following).
Defendant residing abroad: check the rule on territorial jurisdiction and service abroad, and the reconciliation attempt with an absent spouse.
Public prosecution is a main party in all cases concerning the Family Code (Family Code article 3 bis): the file must be communicated to the prosecutor.

Time limit: no limitation period for the khul claim itself as long as the marriage exists; check that no previous divorce judgment already dissolved the marriage and that no other dissolution case is pending (lis pendens).
Appeal: judgments pronouncing divorce, tatliq or khul are not subject to appeal except in their material aspects (Family Code article 57); cassation remains open; check the periods for cassation.

Accessory requests: maintenance during the idda for the wife (articles 61 and following), maintenance of the children (articles 75 and following), from the date of the claim with a possible award for up to one year before (article 80).

Custody: the mother comes first (article 64); the judge decides custody and visitation rights in the khul judgment; custody ends at ten years for a boy (extendable to 16 if the custodian is the mother not remarried) and at marriage age for a girl (article 65).
Housing: the father must provide the custodian with suitable housing or its rent (article 72), the custodian stays in the marital home until the father performs the judgment.

Restitution of the wife's furniture and jewellery (matâ' al-bayt): article 73 on disputes over household goods (the wife's oath or proof, items usual for women); personal property of the wife (article 37 and dowry rules).

Dowry: the dowry is the wife's property; khul does not by itself cancel any unpaid dowry unless the consideration is agreed as its waiver; check if the wife offers to return or waive the dowry as consideration.
Provisional measures during the case (Family Code article 57 bis): the judge may order urgent measures on maintenance, custody, visitation and housing.
Capacity: the wife must have legal capacity; check if she is a minor married with authorisation (article 7) and who represents her.
Proof of the offer: the petition must state the amount offered as consideration; check whether the payment is a condition of the judgment or follows it.
Idda: the idda of the divorced woman (three menstrual cycles or three months, article 58), the wife's right to stay in the marital home during idda; check the start of the idda from the judgment.
Registration: the judgment is transcribed in the civil-status register; the court sends it to the civil-status officer.
Fees and lawyer: in family matters, check whether representation by a lawyer is mandatory at first instance (it is not before the tribunal) and the fees.
Petition formal elements (CPCA article 15): names, addresses, the court, facts and requests, documents; the absence of the marriage certificate makes the claim inadmissible in practice.

Exits: no administrative or commercial exit; check that the marriage is not a foreign marriage needing exequatur or transcription first, and conflict of laws when one spouse is foreign (Civil Code article 12 on dissolution governed by the husband's national law at the time of filing, with article 13 Algerian law if one spouse is Algerian).
Criminal facts (violence, abandonment of the family) may run in parallel; they do not suspend the khul claim unless the civil judgment depends on them.

Amendments to remember: Ordinance 05-02 of 27 February 2005 amended articles 49, 53, 54, 57 bis, 64, 72 and added article 3 bis; Law 08-09 (CPCA) of 25 February 2008 entered into force on 25 April 2009 and organised the family affairs section and the divorce procedure; Law 22-13 amended the CPCA in 2022.
Check whether the wife already filed a tatliq claim on the same facts that was rejected; khul remains available because it needs no cause.
Check if the husband counters with a request for return to the marital home (ruju' / obedience) and how the court decides between them.
Children's maintenance continues independently of the khul; the khul consideration cannot include the waiver of the children's rights (custody and child maintenance belong to the child).
Is the plaintiff the wife, and is there a valid marriage between the parties (contract or judgment proving it)?
Is the marriage registered in the civil-status register, or must proof of marriage be sought first?
Is the claim a khul (wife frees herself for money) and not a tatliq or a divorce at the husband's will?
Does the wife offer a consideration, and is the sum stated in the petition?
Does khul require the husband's consent, or may the court grant it without it?
If the parties disagree on the sum, what limit does the judge apply (the dower of the like)?
Does the wife need to prove any cause or harm?
Which section of the court hears the claim (family affairs section)?
Which court has territorial jurisdiction (place of the conjugal home, or where the custodian lives, etc.)?
Is the territorial rule one of public order?
Is a divorce, tatliq or khul action between the spouses already pending?
Is a conciliation attempt by the judge mandatory, in how many sessions and within what maximum period?
Is the conciliation record required and what happens if the attempt is omitted?
Is there a time limit to file the khul claim, or may it be filed at any time?
Does the public prosecutor have to be joined in the case?
Which elements of the petition are mandatory, and is a lawyer required?
Which documents must be attached (marriage certificate, family record, children's birth extracts)?
Are there children, and does the petition ask for custody, visitation, maintenance and housing for them?
Can maintenance of the idda period be claimed together with khul, or is it waived by the consideration?
Does the wife keep the right to maintenance of the children after khul?
Who is entitled to custody and what is the housing of the custodian?
Does the wife ask to recover her furniture and jewellery, and how does she prove ownership?
Can the consideration include waiving the dower, the maintenance or the custody?
Is the consideration subject to any limit (not exceeding the dower of the like at judgment)?
Is the judgment on khul appealable, and which parts?
Does the appeal suspend enforcement of the dissolution?
Is the judgment provisionally enforceable as to maintenance and custody?
Is the request for provisional measures (maintenance, residence, custody) available during the case?
Which means of proof apply to marriage and to the consideration?
Does the idda start with the final judgment, and is the husband's remarriage right affected?
What if the husband is abroad or his address is unknown?
Which costs and fees apply and who bears them?
